scenes.text: Plug in your phone at 3 a.m., then again at 3 p.m. Same outlet. Different power plants.
U.S. electricity use usually bottoms out around five in the morning, the EIA says.
In 2025, on the Great Plains grid, wind output equaled about 46 percent of demand at 2 a.m., and only about 31 percent at noon.
At noon in Texas, solar averaged 24 gigawatts in the summer of 2025. Two summers earlier, it was 12.
The grid isn't one machine. It's a different machine every hour. The full story is on Other End of the Wire.
